domainTerms.authenticatedWorkspace: signed-in user's selected organization + isolated local inventory/sync; at most one active

scopeNotes: Weighted uncommitted splits: auth service ops, mobile inventory, session-http, openSyncSocket, host-access, product/batch store, scan-phase.
HostAccessPolicy (apps/web/src/host-access.ts) is already designed in .architect/auth-wall — not re-proposed.
Update workflow already has a provider seam (updater-workflow) — not a hotspot for deepening.

topRecommendation.title: Deepen mobile inventory as one authenticated-workspace module
topRecommendation.why: The uncommitted products.ts → inventory-* split left module-level session globals, a shallow barrel, and sync/mutation/lock logic spread across files. Callers and tests bounce; bugs hide in how locks, context, and sync interact. One deep interface for load/mutate/sync of the active authenticated workspace restores locality and gives leverage to ProductsProvider and the scanner.

candidates.title: Deepen mobile inventory as one authenticated-workspace module
candidates.problem: products.ts was carved into five inventory-* modules plus a re-export barrel. Session identity lives as exported mutable module state (activeUserId, organizationIdPromise); locks, snapshot shaping, mutations, and sync still call each other across files. Deleting any one inventory-* file only relocates complexity — deleting the cluster would force one place to own authenticated-workspace inventory again.
candidates.solution: Collapse the inventory cluster behind one deep module that owns session context, serialization locks, local mutations, cache reads, and sync exchange for the active authenticated workspace. Keep platform sync-socket construction as a thin adapter injected at the seam; stop exporting module-level session globals and the shallow products barrel as the public interface.
candidates.benefits: Locality: inventory bugs and auth-context resets concentrate in one module. Leverage: ProductsProvider, scanner writes, and detail screens share one load/mutate/sync interface. Tests: exercise observable snapshot and mutation outcomes through that interface with local KV/secure-store stand-ins, instead of unit-testing lock helpers in isolation.

beforeAfter.before: ProductsProvider / scanner --> products.ts (barrel) --> inventory-session (globals) + inventory-mutations + inventory-sync + inventory-snapshot; sync opens socket via openMobileSyncSocket
beforeAfter.after: ProductsProvider / scanner --> MobileInventory (deep) --seam--> storage adapter + sync transport adapter; internal locks/session/maps stay private

candidates.title: Deepen product scan session; stop testing phase helpers in isolation
candidates.problem: scan-phase.ts is a shallow pure-helper module extracted for tests; real transitions, pending flags, drafts, and camera lifecycle live in use-scan-session. batch-mutation-target is a seven-line pass-through (deletion test: complexity vanishes). Understanding one scan concept requires bouncing across helpers, hook, and write glue.
candidates.solution: Make a deep scan-session module whose interface is capture → review → save (product/batch/quantity), with phase machine and write orchestration inside. Keep Firebase inference behind an injected vision adapter; fold batchMutationTarget into the session or write path rather than a freestanding module.
candidates.benefits: Locality: phase bugs and save races live with the transitions that cause them. Leverage: scan screen and review sheet become thin UI over one session interface. Tests: drive the session through outcomes (idle → review → inventoryReady) with a mock vision adapter; delete shallow scan-phase-only tests that survive only as long as the helper file does.

beforeAfter.before: scan.tsx --> useScanSession --> scan-phase helpers + useBatchWrites --> batchMutationTarget + products mutations; tests target scan-phase only
beforeAfter.after: scan.tsx --> ScanSession (deep) --seam--> vision adapter + inventory writes; UI cards render session view-model; tests cross ScanSession interface

candidates.title: Keep auth ops as private implementation of AuthService
candidates.problem: service.ts is now a thin wiring facade over four make*Ops factories that are only imported by service itself. The split improved file size but risks treating each ops module as a public seam: AuthServiceApi is already the deep interface callers need, while ops files invite tests and imports past that seam.
candidates.solution: Treat login/session/organization/google-identity (and crypto helpers) as internal implementation of AuthService — same package, not separately advertised interfaces. Prefer tests and Effect layers at AuthService; reserve internal seams only where a second adapter (e.g. fake repository) already exists.
candidates.benefits: Locality: auth worker behavior stays findable under AuthService without learning four factory shapes. Leverage: http routes and future callers keep one AuthServiceApi. Tests: replace-don't-layer — cover identify/authenticate/organize through AuthService with local D1/KV stand-ins; avoid a second tree of ops-level tests.

beforeAfter.before: http routes --> AuthService (thin) --> LoginOps | SessionOps | OrganizationOps | GoogleIdentityOps --> repository/ephemeral
beforeAfter.after: http routes --> AuthService (deep interface) with private ops composition inside the layer; repository/ephemeral remain injected adapters

candidates.title: Deepen shared authenticated-workspace session broker
candidates.problem: SessionHttpClient correctly pulled bearer/refresh/serialization into one module, but WebAuthBroker and desktop AuthBroker still duplicate snapshot refresh, online/error mapping, and listener publish logic. Host-specific refresh (cookie vs refresh-token body, persistence) leaks beside shared session semantics.
candidates.solution: Deepen a shared WorkspaceAuthAdapter builder that owns ensure-fresh → GET /api/auth/session → publish/error mapping. Hosts only supply TokenStore, SessionFetch, needsRefresh/refreshSession, and optional persistence hooks as adapters at the seam.
candidates.benefits: Locality: session snapshot rules change once for web and desktop. Leverage: AuthenticatedWorkspace keeps a smaller, more stable auth adapter interface. Tests: cover session adopt/renew/sign-out through the shared broker with in-memory tokens and a fake fetch; host adapters stay thin.

beforeAfter.before: AuthenticatedWorkspace --> WebAuthBroker | Desktop AuthBroker (duplicated refresh/snapshot) --> SessionHttpClient --> fetch
beforeAfter.after: AuthenticatedWorkspace --> SessionBroker (deep) --adapters--> TokenStore + refresh policy + fetch (+ desktop persist); hosts configure only

candidates.title: Separate auth HTTP transport concerns from AuthService
candidates.problem: authRoutes mixes JSON decoding, cookie vs bearer client-kind responses, trusted-origin checks, and AuthService calls in one 350+ line module. Transport policy and domain outcomes share a file, so changing cookie shape risks touching login paths.
candidates.solution: Deepen an auth HTTP transport module that maps requests to AuthService commands and maps TokenSet/errors to browser-cookie or bearer responses. Keep AuthService free of cookie names and Origin rules; inject secureCookies/trustedOrigins only at the transport seam.
candidates.benefits: Locality: cookie/__Host- and CORS/origin rules live with HTTP adapters. Leverage: AuthService stays usable from non-HTTP tests unchanged. Tests: transport tested with a fake AuthService adapter; AuthService tested without HTTP.

beforeAfter.before: HTTP request --> authRoutes (decode + cookies + origins + AuthService calls interleaved)
beforeAfter.after: HTTP request --> AuthHttpTransport --> AuthService; cookie/bearer adapters at transport seam only

candidates.title: Align dual AuthenticatedWorkspace names with domain language
candidates.problem: CONTEXT.md's authenticated workspace maps to two different modules both named AuthenticatedWorkspace: the workspace package's activation orchestrator and persistence's Effect Context tag for scoped org/user/device. Navigating the seam requires knowing which package you are in; AI and humans mis-wire imports.
candidates.solution: Rename or alias so domain language has one primary module name for activation (e.g. keep AuthenticatedWorkspace for the orchestrator) and a distinct name for the persistence Context (e.g. WorkspaceScope / InventoryWorkspace) that still means 'at most one active org+device scope'. Update exports and CONTEXT.md in the same change.
candidates.benefits: Locality: one concept → one name across packages. Leverage: clearer seams between session activation and store scoping. Tests: fewer wrong-import mistakes; existing behaviour unchanged if rename is mechanical.

beforeAfter.before: Callers import AuthenticatedWorkspace from @store/workspace OR @store/persistence (same name, different roles)
beforeAfter.after: Activation module vs persistence scope module have distinct names; CONTEXT.md points to both roles under authenticated workspace

candidates.title: Revisit BatchStore extraction from ProductStore
candidates.problem: makeBatchStore has a single caller (makeProductStore); ProductStore extends BatchStore. Quantity validators are exported from batch-store though nothing outside imports them yet. One-adapter seam (deletion of batch-store mostly moves lines back) — depth may not have increased at the Offline-store interface.
candidates.solution: Either fold batch operations back into a single inventory store implementation while keeping OfflineStore's public interface unchanged, or justify a real second adapter (e.g. tests that construct BatchStore alone). Avoid exporting pure quantity helpers as a freestanding test surface if OfflineStore already covers them.
candidates.benefits: Locality: product+batch mutations that share findProduct/hydration stay together if the split is not earning keep. Leverage: callers already see one Offline store — don't multiply internal interfaces without a second adapter. Tests: keep asserting at Offline-store / ProductStore interface; delete helper-only tests if added.

beforeAfter.before: OfflineStore --> ProductStore extends BatchStore; makeProductStore --> makeBatchStore(findProduct)
beforeAfter.after: OfflineStore --> single InventoryStore implementation (or BatchStore only if a second adapter appears); no hypothetical internal seam

candidates.title: Leave openSyncSocket as a thin shared helper (do not deepen further)
candidates.problem: openSyncSocket only wraps URL construction and SyncTransportError. Platform files remain correct thin adapters (WebSocket headers differ). Deletion test: removing openSyncSocket does not concentrate complexity — it inlines a few lines into three hosts.
candidates.solution: Do not invent a deeper sync-open module. If anything deepens, fold reconnect/session concerns into existing SyncSocketSession rather than thickening openSyncSocket. Keep host connect callbacks as the real adapters.
candidates.benefits: Avoids false depth and extra seams. Locality for live sync stays in SyncSocketSession/runtime. Leverage already exists at session level; open remains a shared one-liner helper.

beforeAfter.before: Hosts --> openSyncSocket(connect) --> SyncSocket; session module handles protocol
beforeAfter.after: Same shape retained; no new module — deepen SyncSocketSession only if reconnect/protocol needs grow
